newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Excel Machine to offer 40-50 mln shares in IPO.
newsitem.headline: Excel Machine to offer 40-50 mln shares in IPO.

text.p: Singapore-based Excel Machine Tools Ltd will offer 40 to 50 million new shares in an initial public offering this week, sources close to the company told Reuters on Monday.
The company, which designs, manufactures and markets machine tools, said last week it had recieved approval in principle to list on the mainboard of the Stock Exchange of Singapore.
"The date of the launch was supposed to be Tuesday but that has not been confirmed," one source said.
Overseas Union Bank was appointed to manage the listing.
Excel, established in 1986, posted a net profit of Singapore $5.1 million last year, more than three times the S$1.6 million recorded in 1992.
Group turnover over the last five years grew at an annual compounded rate of 30 percent to about S$53 million in 1996.
"We make machines, and these make other machines," Robin Lau, its executive chairman and president told reporters last week, referring to his products as "mother machines".
Lau declined to forecast earnings growth for 1997.
It exports machines, which range in cost from S$80,000 to S$300,000, for aerospace, electronics, automobile, mould and die, and medical industries in some 30 countries.
But the company has moved from making traditional metal cutting machines to those that can cut with water jets.
In 1993, it received a S$2 million government grant to develop a new laser-cutting technology and has now produced a machine that can cut, weld and solder metal sheets, Lau said.
The group operates eight subsidiaries in five countries -- Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Hungary and the United States.
Lau said the proceeds from listing would go to regional expansion in India and China, working capital and repayment of bank borrowings.
Analysts said Excel should draw relatively keen interest, depending on the price.
"Retail interest for penny stocks and IPO's have been good for quick punting," Keppel Securities analyst Sim Shyh Yang said.
Others said that in the present bearish market, valuation details would still be analysed closely, although Excel appeared attractive as it is Singapore's only machine-tool company.
